svg.title: 20W dummy load stripboard build reference
svg.desc: Stripboard layout, circuit, parts, build order, bench checks, and modeled RF performance for a DIY version of the K7RHY 20W dummy load.

g.text: component side up • strips run left–right underneath • hole = (column, strip) • 32 columns × 11 strips
both wires ≤ 10 mm, side by side
Resistors lie flat on the board, leads straight down their holes, trimmed short. Adjacent resistors carry opposite currents.
two banks of 4 × 100 Ω in series = 50 Ω
Power = (V + 0.3)² / 25 holds only if D1 drops ≈ 0.3 V at low current; the kit page's calculator assumes the kit's diode.
TP1/TP2 read the peak of the half-voltage tap, as on the PCB kit. C2 is optional but recommended (see §6).
≥ 11 strips × 32 holes, strips along the long side
R1–R8 100 Ω axial resistor, 5 % or better
flameproof metal-oxide, 3 W recommended; each takes ⅛ of the power (§7)
100 V, DO-35. 1N5711 (70 V) also works; avoid 30 V parts (BAT43, BAT85)
≥ 50 V; the "103" disc in the kit
panel or PCB type; solder lug + centre pin
W1–W4 bare straps, W5 insulated wire
TP1, TP2 test pins or flying leads
Check with a meter: no continuity across the cut.
Solder the four bare straps W1–W4 between strips 9 and 10.
Solder R1–R8 flat on the board, leads straight down their holes.
Odd-numbered tops on strip 1, even on strip 2, as drawn; trim leads short.
Solder C2 (col 13) and the two BNC wires (col 12).
Each wire ≤ 10 mm; run them side by side.
Meter the divider before fitting the detector.
Fit D1 (band toward col 29), C1, W5, TP1, TP2.
W5 is insulated; keep it clear of the resistors.
Repeat the checks in §5, then test at low power.
Start at 5 W; check heat after 30 s; stay inside §7.
Cut on strip 10, before D1 is fitted
Diode test, red on strip 9, black on TP1
6. EXPECTED RF PERFORMANCE — MODELED, NOT MEASURED
lumped model of this exact layout; trust it below about 60 MHz
Nominal: ordinary leaded resistors, BNC wires 10 mm. Pessimistic: +40 nH inside each resistor and 20 mm BNC wires — an invented bad case, not a bound.
2 m and 70 cm are not claimed: above ~100 MHz this model leaves out too much. Measure before trusting the board there.
Everything here is a prediction until a NanoVNA sweep of a built board confirms it.
7. POWER LIMITS — RECOMMENDED, NOT YET THERMALLY TESTED
the limit follows the resistors you fit
20 W for up to 30 s, then rest 2 min
13 W for up to 30 s, then rest 2 min
Each resistor takes ⅛ of the power: 20 W is 2.5 W per resistor.
FT8 and other full-duty digital modes count as continuous.
Never above 20 W: D1 sees about 44 V peak inverse there (BAT46 is rated 100 V).
Ventilate any enclosure and keep the load clear of plastic.
These are a design recommendation (2026-10-25), not a measured rating.
